rows.name: Input coupling
rows.question: Does the player's character, as placed in the level at the start, answer to at least two different keys?
rows.definition: A1 holds iff the avatar present at level start is of a class that responds to at least two actions: every class except NullAvatar and MissileAvatar. Fails if no avatar is present.

rows.name: Input coupling
rows.question: Does the player's character, as placed in the level at the start, answer to at least two different keys?
rows.definition: A1 holds iff the avatar present at level start is of a class that responds to at least two actions: every class except NullAvatar and MissileAvatar. Fails if no avatar is present.

rows.name: One controlled object
rows.question: Is the avatar the only thing whose position the player's keys decide?
rows.definition: A2 holds iff exactly one sprite's displacement is a function of the action, the avatar. It fails if the level does not place exactly one avatar sprite at start; if an interaction moves another sprite because the avatar moved into it (bounceForward, pullWithIt with the avatar as partner); and if the avatar's use action creates a sprite (ShootAvatar, FlakAvatar, ShootOnlyAvatar, AimedAvatar, OngoingShootAvatar) [...] A2 also fails wherever an action creates a sprite other than the avatar: an interaction that names an avatar type, in any position, and creates a sprite of a non-avatar type (a spawn effect, cloneSprite, or a transform into a non-avatar type); a transform of the avatar into another avatar type creates no other sprite. [...]

[...]

rows.name: Lattice motion
rows.question: Does each arrow key, when the avatar is not blocked, always move it exactly one square in the same direction, wherever it is and whichever way it faces?
rows.definition: A3 holds iff each movement action, when not blocked, shifts the avatar by one constant vector whatever its position, facing and history: MovingAvatar, HorizontalAvatar, VerticalAvatar and FlakAvatar at speed 1; OrientedAvatar and ShootAvatar only with rotateInPlace=False. It fails for every other avatar class, for a speed other than 1, and where an interaction moves the avatar (teleportToExit, wrapAround, pullWithIt, bounceForward, windGust, slipForward, conveySprite, attractGaze).

rows.name: Lattice motion
rows.question: Does each arrow key, when the avatar is not blocked, always move it exactly one square in the same direction, wherever it is and whichever way it faces?
rows.definition: A3 holds iff each movement action, when not blocked, shifts the avatar by one constant vector whatever its position, facing and history: MovingAvatar, HorizontalAvatar, VerticalAvatar and FlakAvatar at speed 1; OrientedAvatar and ShootAvatar only with rotateInPlace=False. It fails for every other avatar class, for a speed other than 1, and where an interaction moves the avatar (teleportToExit, wrapAround, pullWithIt, bounceForward, windGust, slipForward, conveySprite, attractGaze).

rows.name: A fixed set of blockers
rows.question: Is every step that the avatar cannot take stopped by a sprite that never moves on its own and that only the player's own actions can create, remove or move?
rows.definition: A4 holds iff every move without effect is explained by a sprite that blocks the avatar (stepBack or undoAll with the avatar), every blocking type is of a class that never moves on its own (Immovable, Passive, Door, Resource, ResourcePack, SpawnPoint, SpawnPointMultiSprite, Portal, SpriteProducer), and blocking sprites are created, removed or moved only through the avatar's own actions: by interactions whose names include only agent-driven sprites, which are the avatar, the sprites its use action creates, and stationary-class sprites that only those push or pull. A sprite that kills on contact does not block. [...] "With the avatar" is applied with the avatar named first. A blocker transformed into another blocking type in place counts as created and removed [...] A blocking relation that depends on the avatar's subtype holds A4, because the set of obstacles does not change during play. [...] The generator counts a name as standing for agent-driven sprites when every type it can place is agent-driven [...] The first clause is checked through every undoAll line that cancels the avatar's move, and a chain push or an edge wrap of a pushed box counts as the avatar's own [...]

rows.name: A place goal
rows.question: Is the only way to win to reach one single goal object that only the avatar can remove?
rows.definition: A5 holds iff the only winning condition is a SpriteCounter with limit 0 on one sprite type, the level holds exactly one sprite of that type, and every interaction that removes it has the avatar or an avatar subtype as partner; a precondition met elsewhere is recorded and keeps A5 holding.

rows.definition: A4 holds iff every move without effect is explained by a sprite that blocks the avatar (stepBack or undoAll with the avatar), every blocking type is of a class that never moves on its own (Immovable, Passive, Door, Resource, ResourcePack, SpawnPoint, SpawnPointMultiSprite, Portal, SpriteProducer), and blocking sprites are created, removed or moved only through the avatar's own actions: by interactions whose names include only agent-driven sprites, which are the avatar, the sprites its use action creates, and stationary-class sprites that only those push or pull. A sprite that kills on contact does not block. [...] "With the avatar" is applied with the avatar named first. A blocker transformed into another blocking type in place counts as created and removed [...] A blocking relation that depends on the avatar's subtype holds A4, because the set of obstacles does not change during play. [...] The generator counts a name as standing for agent-driven sprites when every type it can place is agent-driven [...] The first clause is checked through every undoAll line that cancels the avatar's move, and a chain push or an edge wrap of a pushed box counts as the avatar's own [...]

rows.name: A place goal
rows.question: Is the only way to win to reach one single goal object that only the avatar can remove?
rows.definition: A5 holds iff the only winning condition is a SpriteCounter with limit 0 on one sprite type, the level holds exactly one sprite of that type, and every interaction that removes it has the avatar or an avatar subtype as partner; a precondition met elsewhere is recorded and keeps A5 holding.
